meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale. Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook, and was anyone going to call me first?
Don't thank me yet, Hale. Answer the question: who decided on the zero, and why did Owen find out from his phone?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn and that nothing go on Owen's record, and I expect an explanation of who decided on it and why I was not called first. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with the zero still standing and nothing agreed.
What moved her: nothing.
What cost ground: "Thanks for coming in." gave her nothing, and it let her put the unanswered question about the zero back on you.
Try next time: after her first question, own in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then put a dated document in front of her.
